brief.regime_label: HAWKISH-HOLD BEAR-STEEPENER · EUR WAS SQUEEZE · BDC SOFTWARE BIFURCATION
brief.headline: Warsh's hawkish 10-2 FOMC hold locks floating-rate borrowers at high coupons while Fitch's European CLO 'triple squeeze' and [[F111]] BDC software stress deepen mezzanine dispersion.
brief.summary: Overnight's hawkish FOMC hold at [[F91]] (two hike dissents plus Chairman Warsh's SOMA balance-sheet governance pivot) bear-steepened sovereign curves — dropping fixed-rate IG `LQD` to [[F108]] ([[F109]] on the day, [[F110]] vs 52W high) while floating-rate `JAAA` held rock-solid at [[F79]] ([[F80]] vs 52W high). Beneath senior CLO protection, subterranean credit dispersion intensified across four channels: (1) Fitch European CLO surveillance revealed average WAS compressed to [[F14]] with just [[F100]] of WAS cushion and [[F103]] of sub-cushion deals trapped in a 'triple squeeze', even as late-October European new-issue AAA drifted to [[F98]] and US BB spreads widened [[F107]] to [[F65]] (a [[F66]] AAA–BB basis); (2) Altice International's [[F72]] NY Commercial Division lawsuit and VMO2/VodafoneZiggo contagion ([[F78]] TLB mark) pressure European telecom pools; (3) Thames Water locked in its 16 October Class B wipeout ([[F33]] equity) while seeking an upsized [[F104]] super-senior bridge ahead of L&VW's [[F106]] RP2 plan; and (4) Software climbed to [[F111]] of all stressed BDC investments alongside Fitch's junk BB+ rating on `FSK` ([[F112]] software) and Moody's warning on circular AI infrastructure debt across the [[F113]] data-centre cycle.

decisions.impact: Insulates portfolio carry from Warsh curve steepening while blocking priming, regulatory, and SaaS PIK-conversion losses.

decisions.ask: Screen European CLO mezzanine against Fitch's [[F103]] 'triple squeeze' cohort (deals below [[F100]] WAS, [[F101]] WARF, and [[F102]] WARR cushions) alongside combined VMO2/VodafoneZiggo obligor weights.
decisions.why: European CLO WAS has compressed to [[F14]] ([[F100]] average cushion, [[F103]] triple-squeeze tail) just as late-October EUR AAA drifted to [[F98]] and telecom contagion hit VMO2 ([[F75]]) and VodafoneZiggo ([[F78]]).
decisions.impact: Prevents allocation to post-RP or telecom-concentrated European mezzanine tranches vulnerable to Fitch 'F'-note downgrades.

decisions.ask: Require non-circular tenant recourse and GPU-amortisation matching before underwriting any data-centre ABS/CMBS or private credit AI infrastructure facility.

topics.title: CLO Liability Divergence, US BB Widening & Fitch's European 'Triple Squeeze'
topics.thesis: US tier-1 AAA holds tight at [[F64]] even as US BB widened [[F107]] to [[F65]] (a [[F66]] AAA–BB basis), while in Europe late-October new-issue AAA drifted to [[F98]] and Fitch surveillance reveals portfolio WAS compressed to [[F14]] with just [[F100]] of WAS cushion and [[F103]] of low-WAS deals trapped in a 'triple squeeze'.
topics.verdict: LONG AAA/AA & POST-RP SENIOR · VETO TRIPLE-SQUEEZE & POST-RP BB
topics.stack_note: Tranche shares are an illustrative CLO 2.0 capital stack; live market anchors are European AAA at [[F10]]–[[F98]], US tier-1 AAA at [[F64]], and US BB at [[F65]] ([[F66]] basis). Use the interactive stress simulator below to test how default rates and CCC buckets above [[F42]] erode Equity and B/BB tranches while leaving AAA subordination intact.
topics.signal: European CLO issuance reached [[F01]] across [[F02]] year-to-date through September 2026; September printed [[F03]] across [[F04]], split between [[F05]] of new issue ([[F06]]) at [[F07]] AAA and [[F08]] of refinancings and resets ([[F09]]) at [[F10]] AAA (a [[F11]] refi/reset discount), before heavy Q4 supply from [[F12]] (against a [[F13]] full-year refi/reset forecast) nudged late-October European new-issue AAA prints to [[F98]]. Newly harvested Fitch European CLO surveillance narrows Gap G1: average portfolio Weighted Average Spread (WAS) has compressed to [[F14]] ([[F99]] below the ten-year average), leaving the average WAS cushion at just [[F100]] alongside a [[F101]] WARF cushion and [[F102]] WARR cushion — with [[F103]] of sub-cushion deals in a 'triple squeeze' where Fitch downgrades target junior 'F' notes while equity cash-on-cash distributions print [[F15]]. In the US, September BSL issuance softened to [[F62]] across [[F63]] with tier-1 AAA firm at [[F64]], but tier-1 BB widened [[F107]] in October to [[F65]], stretching the AAA–BB basis to [[F66]] against Fitch's US OC split ([[F67]] Senior / [[F68]] Junior OC in reinvesting deals at WARF [[F69]], versus [[F70]] Senior / [[F71]] Junior OC in post-reinvestment deals). On the live 29 October FMP tape, `JAAA` holds at [[F79]] ([[F80]] vs 52-week high) and `JBBB` trades at [[F81]] ([[F82]] vs 52-week high). Direct Form NPORT-P XML parsing across [[F134]] confirms zero sub-99 marks in `JAAA` versus [[F133]] of `JBBB` mezzanine CLO tranches marked below 99.00.
topics.mechanism: Two structural squeezes now separate senior from junior CLO risk on both sides of the Atlantic. In the US, sequential post-reinvestment AAA amortisation builds a [[F70]] Senior OC windfall while starving post-RP Junior OC to [[F71]], driving [[F107]] of BB widening to a [[F66]] AAA–BB basis. In Europe, loan repricings compressed portfolio WAS to [[F14]] ([[F100]] cushion) just as Q4 new-issue AAA drifted to [[F98]]; managers trapped in Fitch's [[F103]] 'triple squeeze' lack the spread, rating, and recovery buffers to trade out of deteriorating credits without tripping par or Junior OC tests.

heuristics.text: At standard CLO 2.0 leverage of [[F56]], each percentage point of uncompensated default loss erodes roughly [[F56]] its weight in equity par; in US post-RP deals ([[F71]] Jr OC) and Fitch's [[F103]] European triple-squeeze cohort ([[F100]] WAS cushion), CCC migration above [[F42]] rapidly trips diversion.

Interest-coverage triage under the [[F91]] Fed floor: borrowers below [[F57]] enter the cash-flow red zone; below [[F58]] seek PIK amendments (feeding [[F44]] BDC PIK and `FSK`'s junk BB+ downgrade); below [[F59]] face RCF draws or LMEs ([[F96]] estimated 12-month hazard).
